This supplies the finite-local-constancy criterion in the classical torsion constructibility chain: 0GKW invokes 0GKV, whose case (a) uses specialization invariance and finite stalks. title: Lifting geometric specializations to strict local schemes
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $t,s\in S$ satisfy $s\in\overline{\{t\}}$, and choose geometric points $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_t\to S$ and $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_s\to S$ over $t,s$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. For the strict local scheme $S_{(\bar s)}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] with structural map $p:S_{(\bar s)}\to S$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map], there exists a morphism $a:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_t\to S_{(\bar s)}$ satisfying $p\circ a=\bar t$.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ containing $s$. The point $t$ also belongs to $U$, since every open containing a specialization contains its generizations. Write $\mathfrak m,\mathfrak r\subset R$ for $s,t$; then $\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak m$. For every affine pointed neighbourhood $(V,\bar v)$ of $\bar s$ over $S$, shrink inside the open inverse image of $U$ using the affine-shrinking lemma. Thus it receives a pointed map from an affine neighbourhood whose structural map factors through $U$. The full subcategory of these neighbourhoods is cofiltered and has the same opposite-indexed ring colimit by the initial-full-subcategory lemma. Its objects and arrows are exactly the affine pointed neighbourhoods of $\bar s$ considered as a point of $U$: factorization through an open subscheme is unique. Consequently the same colimit ring $H$ represents both strict local schemes, and compatibility of the coprojections identifies $p$ with $\operatorname{Spec}H\to U\hookrightarrow S$. In particular $H$ is an ind-etale $R$-algebra: it is the filtered colimit of the etale affine coordinate algebras of those neighbourhoods.

source.place: Tag 0GJ5, remark-can-lift; affine-neighbourhood reduction, expanded using Tag 04HX, lemma-describe-etale-local-ring

proof.text: Apply the geometric strict-henselization local-presentation lemma to $U$, its geometric point $\bar s$, and the structural map $R\to H$ from step 1. It gives a prime $\mathfrak q\subset R$, $A=R_{\mathfrak q}$, a separable closure $K$ of its residue field, and an $A$-algebra structure making $H$ an algebraic strict henselization of $A$, with $R\to A\to H$ equal to the structural map. The triples-presentation lemma expresses this as a universal colimit of etale residue triples over the maximal ideal of $A$, with the prescribed structural map. The strict-henselization-triples theorem identifies the unique maximal ideal of $H$ and shows its contraction to $A$ is the maximal ideal of $A$; its contraction to $R$ is therefore $\mathfrak q$. Apply clause (1) of strict-henselization functoriality with $g=\mathrm{id}_U$: the geometric structural map sends the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}H$ to $s$, so that same contraction is $\mathfrak m$. Hence $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak m$, and the faithfully-flat strict-henselization lemma now gives faithful flatness of the compatible map $R_{\mathfrak m}\to H$.

source.place: Tag 0GJ5, remark-can-lift; faithfully flat local-ring map, using Tags 04HX, 04GW, 04GP and 07QM(1)

proof.text:
The prime $\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak m$ defines the prime $\mathfrak rR_{\mathfrak m}$ of $R_{\mathfrak m}$, with contraction $\mathfrak r$: a fraction $x/u$ with $u
otin\mathfrak m$ lies in this ideal exactly when $x\in\mathfrak r$. Indeed the localized quotient is $(R\setminus\mathfrak m)^{-1}(R/\mathfrak r)$, a nonzero domain since $\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak m$. If $x/u$ maps to zero, some $v
otin\mathfrak m$ has $vx\in\mathfrak r$; primality and $v
otin\mathfrak r$ give $x\in\mathfrak r$. Apply faithful-flat surjectivity of spectra to $R_{\mathfrak m}	o H$. We obtain a prime $P\subset H$ contracting to $\mathfrak rR_{\mathfrak m}$, and therefore to $\mathfrak r$ in $R$. Let $t^{\prime}$ be the corresponding point of $\operatorname{Spec}H$; the map $p$ sends it to $t$.

source.place: Tag 0GJ5, remark-can-lift; lifting the ordinary point, using Tag 00HQ, lemma-ff-rings

proof.text: Put $k=\kappa(\mathfrak r)=\kappa(t)$ and $B=H\otimes_R k$. By ind-etale stability, the ind-etale $R$-algebra $H$ gives an ind-etale, hence weakly etale, $k$-algebra $B$. The fibre-ring identification gives $B= (R\setminus\mathfrak r)^{-1}H/\mathfrak r(R\setminus\mathfrak r)^{-1}H$. Since $P\cap R=\mathfrak r$, localizing $P$ and then quotienting defines a prime $Q$ of $B$. Its local ring is $H_P/\mathfrak rH_P$ and its residue field is $H_P/PH_P=\kappa(t^{\prime})$: localizing first at $R\setminus\mathfrak r$ and then at $Q$ inverts precisely the remaining elements outside $P$, and quotienting by $\mathfrak r$ does not change the final residue quotient. These identifications respect the map $k\to\kappa(t^{\prime})$. Apply the weakly-etale-over-a-field lemma to $B/k$; its residue field at $Q$, hence $\kappa(t^{\prime})$, is separable algebraic over $k$.

source.place: Tag 0GJ5, remark-can-lift; algebraic residue-field extension, expanded via more-algebra.tex, Tag 092Q, lemma-absolutely-flat-over-field

proof.text: The given $\bar t$ determines the embedding $\iota:k\to\Omega_t$. Since $\kappa(t^{\prime})/k$ is algebraic and $\Omega_t$ is algebraically closed, the algebraic-extension embedding lemma gives $j:\kappa(t^{\prime})\to\Omega_t$ extending $\iota$. The composite $H_P\to H_P/PH_P=\kappa(t^{\prime})\xrightarrow{j}\Omega_t$ has kernel $PH_P$, because $j$ is an injective field homomorphism; the maximal ideal of $\Omega_t$ is zero, so this is a local homomorphism. The morphism-from-a-local-spectrum bijection, applied to $\operatorname{Spec}H$ and the local ring $\Omega_t$, gives $a:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_t\to\operatorname{Spec}H=S_{(\bar s)}$ with image $t^{\prime}$ and this local-ring map. The composite $p\circ a$ has image $t$ and residue-field map $j|_k=\iota$; its local-ring map is thus $\mathcal O_{S,t}\to k\xrightarrow{\iota}\Omega_t$, the one of $\bar t$. Injectivity of the same local-spectrum bijection for $S$ gives $p\circ a=\bar t$.
